topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, outlines the lecture series, and presents the key learning outcomes regarding cancer etiology.

topics.label: Principles of Cancer Biology and Sources of Mutation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and discuss the intrinsic cellular processes and inherited predispositions that generate oncogenic mutations.

topics.label: Environmental Carcinogens and Epidemiological Patterns
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine common environmental exposures and the global epidemiological data linking geographic variations to specific cancer risks.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infectious agents contribute to malignancy, featuring Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed case study of viral and co-infectious etiology.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Physical and Chemical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific chemical compounds and ultraviolet radiation are metabolized and form mutagenic DNA adducts or lesions.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion and Non-Mutagenic Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the distinction between cancer initiation and promotion, focusing on how non-mutagenic stimuli and chronic inflammation drive clonal expansion.

topics.label: Host Tissue Susceptibility and Developmental Stage
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how cellular proliferation during specific developmental stages and hormonal states dictates tissue vulnerability to carcinogens.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics overview the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental methodologies used to establish whether agents are carcinogenic.
